subject: Production access curtailment impacting NovaBio inference (urgent)
messages:
From: Claire Watson <claire.watson@novabio.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production: sudden access curtailment impacting inference

Jasmine —

We started seeing a big uptick in errors and latency to the Redwood endpoints for our inference traffic around 08:55 UTC this morning. Symptoms:
- 429 "rate limit exceeded" returned for about 18% of requests for ~25 minutes
- Median p50 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms; P95 > 3s for several minutes
- No sudden traffic spike on our side (our telemetry is flat)

Attached is a short log extract (nova_api_logs_20281004.txt) showing repeated 429s and a few 503s. This is impacting live customers and our batch jobs are backing up. Can you confirm whether this is a NovaBio-side quota or something on Redwood's policy side? We need urgent help.

—Claire
Claire Watson
Director, Platform Operations
NovaBio

Attachments: nova_api_logs_20281004.txt (text)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Watson <claire.watson@novabio.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden access curtailment impacting inference

Folks — looping in infra and support. Claire reports 429s + latency hit for NovaBio (NB-4321). Customer telemetry does not show a traffic spike. Please triage urgently and advise mitigation (temporary burst lift, routing to fallback variant, etc.).

Customer impact: production inference degraded, customer-facing incidents. They are asking for immediate remediation and a timeline for a permanent fix.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: quick root cause + recommended short-term mitigation (increase burst cap or route)
- Karthik/Rishi: if we need a policy exception, can we apply a scoped emergency change for 24h and who approves?
- Vanessa: FYI on customer escalation; you may want to engage sales leadership for credit/PR.

I attached the log Claire sent. I'll update the customer once we have a mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Watson <claire.watson@novabio.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden access curtailment impacting inference

Jasmine / team — quick update from triage:

What I see: policy evaluation logs show NovaBio's consumer policy was unintentionally migrated with an incorrect burst window value during last night's config rollout. The burst-window parameter was interpreted as seconds in the new config but the migration wrote it as "1" (intended to be 60). In short, the effective burst window became 1s instead of 60s which caused token-bucket enforcement to fire much more aggressively under their steady traffic pattern. That produced the 429s and the higher queuing/latency when requests were forced into the lower-tier path.

Immediate mitigations performed (applied 10:02 UTC):
- Temporarily raised NovaBio burst cap by +3x for the next 24h to stop enforced drops
- Enabled fallback routing to the compatible model-variant in our secondary region for high-latency flows
- Scanned recent config commits and flagged the migration script that erroneously wrote the window value

I've attached a snapshot of the policy entry we saw (policy_config_snapshot.json) and a short mitigation checklist (mitigation_commands.txt).

Next steps (24–72h):
- Roll back the faulty migration and redeploy a corrected policy writer (Rishi/Karthik)
- Run a synthetic traffic replay to validate steady-state behavior
- Follow up with NovaBio on a postmortem and next release schedule

Status: change applied; I'm watching metrics.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: policy_config_snapshot.json, mitigation_commands.txt
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Billing <billing@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Subject: Emergency exception request: NovaBio burst-cap increase

Marissa / Billing — FYI, Marcus applied a scoped temporary burst increase for NovaBio (NB-4321) to stop a production degradation caused by a config migration error. The customer is on a committed Dedicated plan; we risk breaching a 99.9% SLA if this continues.

Requesting approval for the following (one-time emergency exception):
- Apply 24-hour elevated burst cap (already in place)
- Issue a goodwill credit up to $7,500 to offset impact to their customers (billing to confirm)

Please confirm approval or escalate to finance leadership. I'll coordinate customer communications once billing confirms.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, NA
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Claire Watson <claire.watson@novabio.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden access curtailment impacting inference

Claire / team — following Marcus's mitigation, observed telemetry shows error rate down to ~0.5% and latency back to baseline within ~4 minutes of the change. The change we applied was a scoped config override (nova-burst-cap: +3x) at 10:02 UTC and enabling regional fallback for requests exceeding latency thresholds.

Dashboard (live): https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/nb-4321/production-errors (internal)

Planned: we'll keep the emergency override for 24h while we patch the migration script and run a replay. I'll post a follow-up when the rollback and validation are complete.

—Karthik Iyer
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
